covers: The 16 registers of the AY-3-8910 family behind its address latch

left_out.why: the second register bank exists only on the ay8930 in extended mode; the types of this chip have a 4-bit register latch and the bank offset is always 0

entries.name: tone period
entries.description: Tone period of channels A, B and C: the fine byte at even offsets, the coarse nibble at odd offsets.
entries.behaviour: 0x00, 0x02 and 0x04 are the low 8 bits for channels A, B and C; 0x01, 0x03 and 0x05 are bits 8 to 11 in their low four bits, and bits 4 to 7 are stored and unused. A period of 0 acts as 1. A read returns the stored byte; type ay8910 alone masks the coarse registers to 0x0F.

entries.name: noise period
entries.description: Period of the noise generator, 5 bits.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 4 are the noise period and 0 acts as 1. Bits 5 to 7 are stored and unused. A read returns the stored byte; type ay8910 alone masks it to 0x1F.

entries.name: mixer and port control
entries.description: Switches tone and noise off per channel and sets the direction of I/O ports A and B.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 2 switch off tone on channels A, B and C and bits 3 to 5 noise, 1 meaning off. Bit 6 makes port A an output (1) or input (0), bit 7 port B. A change of either calls that port's write callback with the latch when it turns output, 0xFF and an empty mask when input.

entries.name: mixer readback
entries.description: Returns the mixer and port direction byte as written.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the stored byte on every type, with no masking. The direction bits are only what was written, not the state of the pins.

entries.name: channel volume
entries.description: Volume of channels A, B and C: a fixed 4-bit level or the envelope.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 3 are the fixed level and bit 4 takes the level from the envelope generator instead, shared by all three channels. Bits 5 to 7 are stored and unused; type ay8910 alone masks a read to 0x1F. With tone and noise both off in 0x07 the output holds this level as a constant.

entries.name: envelope period
entries.description: The 16-bit envelope period: low byte at 0x0B, high byte at 0x0C.
entries.behaviour: Both bytes are fully used, and a read returns them as stored. A period of 0 steps on every tick, like 1 on a YM-type chip (ym2149, ym3439, ymz284, ymz294, sunsoft_5b_sound) and twice as fast as 1 on an AY-type chip. Writing them does not restart the envelope; only a write to 0x0D does.

entries.name: envelope shape
entries.description: Shape bits of the envelope: continue, attack, alternate and hold; writing them starts the envelope.
entries.behaviour: Bit 3 is continue, bit 2 attack (rising), bit 1 alternate and bit 0 hold; with continue clear it acts as hold set and alternate equal to attack. Every write restarts the envelope, even of the same value. It has 16 steps on AY-type chips (ay8910, ay8912, ay8913) and 32, twice as fast, on the YM-type ones.

entries.name: envelope shape readback
entries.description: Returns the stored shape byte, not the live envelope level.
entries.behaviour: Bits 4 to 7 are stored and unused: type ay8910 returns them as 0 and the other types return them as written. No register returns the running envelope or counters.

entries.name: port A output
entries.description: The port A output latch, 8 bits.
entries.behaviour: The byte is stored. With bit 6 of 0x07 set it goes to the port A write callback, or a warning is logged when none is bound. With bit 6 clear it is not sent now, and the stored byte goes out when the port later becomes an output.

entries.name: port A input
entries.description: Reads the 8 pins of port A through the port A read callback.
entries.behaviour: The callback is called and its value returned whatever bit 6 of 0x07 says, so an output port still reads the pins. With none bound the last stored value is returned. Binding a callback on a type without port A is fatal at start: ay8913, ymz284, ymz294 and sunsoft_5b_sound have none.

entries.name: port B output
entries.description: The port B output latch, 8 bits.
entries.behaviour: The byte is stored. With bit 7 of 0x07 set it goes to the port B write callback, or a warning is logged when none is bound. With bit 7 clear it is not sent now, and the stored byte goes out when the port later becomes an output.

entries.name: port B input
entries.description: Reads the 8 pins of port B through the port B read callback.
entries.behaviour: The callback is called and its value returned whatever bit 7 of 0x07 says, so an output port still reads the pins. With none bound the last stored value is returned. Binding a callback on a type without port B is fatal at start: ay8912, ay8913, ymz284, ymz294 and sunsoft_5b_sound have none.
